title: Implement bounded audio ring buffer
description:
Create a lock-free, bounded, single-producer single-consumer audio ring buffer suitable for use inside a PipeWire realtime callback.

Before editing, inspect:
- Any existing files under src/audio/ for conventions, include style, and namespace usage.
- CMakeLists.txt at the project root and under src/ for how source files are registered.

Do not infer APIs, schemas, behavior, or file contents; inspect the referenced files first.

Implement AudioRingBuffer as a templated or float/int32-based SPSC ring buffer with:
- A fixed power-of-two capacity set at construction time.
- A lockfree write() callable from the PipeWire realtime thread (no allocation, no blocking, no exceptions).
- A read()/consume() for the writer thread to drain samples.
- Overflow detection: write() must return a status or count indicating how many frames were dropped; it must never block or grow.
- Underrun detection: read() must report when fewer frames are available than requested.
- Memory ordering via std::atomic with acquire/release semantics; no mutexes.
- Static assertion or comment confirming the type is trivially copyable.

Do not include any file I/O, compression, Qt headers, or PipeWire headers in this unit. The ring buffer is a pure data structure with no external dependencies beyond the C++ standard library.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY the files listed in this task's allowed_write_paths.
acceptance_criteria: src/audio/AudioRingBuffer.hpp exists and declares the ring buffer class with write() and read() methods
write() is lock-free: no std::mutex, no std::lock_guard, no blocking syscalls, no dynamic allocation in the write path
Overflow is observable: write() returns a value or sets a flag indicating dropped frames when the buffer is full
Underrun is observable: read() returns a value indicating fewer frames available than requested
No #include of Qt, PipeWire, libsndfile, or FLAC headers appears in either file
g++ -std=c++20 -fsyntax-only src/audio/AudioRingBuffer.cpp -I src passes or cmake --build build compiles the unit
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: modify any file outside src/audio/AudioRingBuffer.hpp and src/audio/AudioRingBuffer.cpp
include Qt, PipeWire, libsndfile, or FLAC headers
use std::mutex or any blocking synchronization primitive
perform dynamic memory allocation in write() or read() hot paths

allowed: choose between templated and fixed-type ring buffer
choose power-of-two masking vs modulo for index wrapping
choose between returning status codes or frame counts for overflow/underrun
forbidden: add dynamic resizing or growable buffer
add file I/O or logging in the data path
